Alex (product): Priya, saw your note about ACME's unpredictable monthly usage — they want credit-based protection against big spikes. Can you paste the ask?
Priya (sales): They want a customer-friendly plan: a reserved baseline (commit) + a pool of credits that auto-apply when monthly tokens exceed baseline. Prefer per-token cap for overage. Want legal to sign off asap.
Megan (support): They're also worried about throttling during spikes — support ticket #4532. Need SLA clarity: what happens when credits run out mid-month?
Dan (finance): Two quick things: 1) credits are revenue-recognition heavy, need explicit invoicing rules; 2) we should model unit economics — credits at 0.75x list maybe ok for small pilots.
Riley (eng): From infra side, auto-applying credits is config-only, but per-token capping + graceful fallback requires a runtime check + routing change. Estimated 2 sprints if we do a lightweight flow, 4+ if we want per-request billing certainty.
Alex (product): Goal for this thread: decide triage / backlog priority and define minimal scope to unblock sales. Proposal: pilot with manual credit top-ups handled by finance (low infra work) vs automated credits (higher infra). Thoughts?
Priya (sales): Pilot needs to be quick. Customer wants autonomy but will accept manual process for 2 months. Prioritize manual pilot so we can close the deal this quarter.
Dan (finance): Manual top-ups workable. We'll issue a credit invoice and track consumption in our billing view. Need product to provide a usage export (CSV) weekly. Low lift?
Riley (eng): Weekly CSV export is trivial (existing billing endpoints). Manual apply flow: support/ops clicks "apply credit" to customer account — small UI + ops auth. Estimate 1 sprint frontend + 1 for ops playbook.
Alex (product): Ok agreement: short-term pilot = manual credit top-ups + weekly usage export + documented ops playbook. Long-term scope = automated credit pool + per-token overage cap + UI for self-serve. We need acceptance criteria to move long-term to backlog. Proposed acceptance for pilot:
Alex (product): ```
- Pilot contract executed and credit invoice sent
- Weekly export delivered to Finance for 8 weeks
- No more than 2 incidents where credits were applied manually outside playbook
- Support runbook verified
``` 
Priya (sales): That works. Timeline: invoice + pilot onboarding within 2 weeks.
Dan (finance): I'll prep invoice template and GL codes. Also request a small price test: credits priced at 0.8x for pilot, and a per-token overage ceiling of 1.2x list if auto-overage ever triggers.
Riley (eng): Noted. For backlog, please create a JIRA with these labels: pricing-pilot, billing-export, ops-playbook, followup-automation. Link when created.
Alex (product): Created PROD-9876 and linked to customer record. https://jira.internal/PROD-9876
pricing-bot: New ticket PROD-9876 assigned to Alex (product) and tagged pricing-pilot.
Megan (support): I'll draft the ops playbook and run a runbook test with staging within 5 days.
Priya (sales): Thanks, team. I'll confirm with the customer and push signature.
Alex (product): Next steps: 1) Finance to send invoice (Dan) 2) Support to draft runbook (Megan) 3) Eng to enable weekly export + small UI for ops (Riley) 4) Sales to confirm contract (Priya). Revisit automation scope after pilot metrics (cost delta, incidents, churn risk).
Riley (eng): One caveat — if we see sustained >30% month-over-month variance across many customers, we should fast-track automation. Call that a threshold.
Dan (finance): Agreed. I'll monitor revenue leakage and unit economics and report after 4 weeks.
Priya (sales): Will add to customer kickoff doc. :thumbsup:
Alex (product): Great. Closing thread — will update PROD-9876 with timelines. Thanks everyone.
